hook.text: The first record with The Obsessed singer Scott "Wino" Weinrich on vocals, cut in a Redondo Beach studio.

facts.label: Recorded
facts.value: 1986, at Total Access Recording in Redondo Beach, California

facts.label: Players
facts.value: Scott "Wino" Weinrich (vocals), Dave Chandler (guitar), Mark Adams (bass), Bill Linnane (piano), Armando Acosta (drums)

sentences.text: The sound has been described as rooted in early Black Sabbath, and Paul Kott of AllMusic said the band was looking back on the 1970s.
Kott also saw the band's slow, heavy music as having little commercial viability at the time, and its commitment to that sound went against the L.A. glam metal of the day.
Dave Chandler wrote the music for every song, and Scott Reagers and Robert Gonzales share credit on the lyrics for two of them.
Michael Lardie and Jim Mancuso were the engineers.
The riffs are slow and sludgy, and the songs drop the galloping beat that traditional heavy metal often uses.
In 1987 SST put the album out on CD with three tracks from the Thirsty and Miserable EP added.
The band's compilation Heavier Than Thou holds every song from this album except The War Starter.
On 11 April 2009 the band played Dying Inside in New Orleans, with Phil Anselmo appearing as a guest.

listen_for.text: It is a cover of a Black Flag song.
